sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: State threats and AI - Key takeaways from MI5 chief's speech MI5 is devoting more resource to countering state threats than during the Cold War, the head of the intelligence service has said.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: Sir Ken McCallum said threats from foreign adversaries had quadrupled in the last decade, with Russia "aggressor number one" as well as increased Iran-linked aggression against Jewish sites and military bases.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: At an annual speech in London, MI5's chief said Russia was waging hybrid warfare at a time when AI was "supercharging the cyber-security contest between attackers and defenders".
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: He also warned of rising threats from "extreme right-wing terrorism" and said MI5 had "caught terrorists seeking to exploit AI," including by integrating the technology with drones.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: He said the biggest threat from the misuse of AI was extremist groups using the technology to harness new and existing bioweapons.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: However, he noted that work countering terrorism and state threats was now "pretty much of equal scale" which he described as a "huge shift" in recent years.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: Sir Ken said Russia had stopped short of "conventional conflict" against Nato and is instead trying to unsettle European countries while its progress in its full-scale invasion of Ukraine is "minimal and horrifically costly".
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: Hybrid warfare or hybrid attacks are loose terms which tend to describe non-military methods, for example cyber-attacks, sabotage or misinformation, designed to exert pressure and destabilise an adversary.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: These are quite often employed using proxies, but Russia always denies involvement in such attacks despite growing evidence to the contrary.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: Sir Ken said MI5 successes in identifying and expelling Russian spies from the UK had left the Kremlin dependent on paying proxies for attempted attacks.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: "With its traditional covert footprint eviscerated by almost 1,000 expulsions since the invasion, the Kremlin's global toolkit is weak, he said.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: "So we see them scrambling to pay criminals to do their bidding." He added: "These are not the actions of a great power with the strategic upper hand." His comments come as a growing number of leaders across Europe have warned Russia may be preparing attacks to test their commitment to supporting Ukraine.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: Asked after the speech about Prime Minister Andy Burnham's recent comments that Russia interfered with the Brexit referendum , Sir Ken said it was "not new news" that there had been attempts from Moscow but distinguished between "interference attempted" and "outcome achieved".
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: He said it was a matter of public record that there were pieces in Russian media and "so-called internet trolls and bot farms" seeking to influence the Brexit debate, but also stressed that the result of the 2016 referendum was "not in dispute".
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: He added that he was "worried" about the the ongoing debate on Russian interference.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: "I am a little bit anxious that we don't play into our adversaries' hands by making these trolls look 10ft tall," he told reporters.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: Sir Ken McCallum gave his annual address at MI5's headquarters in central London Meanwhile, Sir Ken warned that Iran is also expanding a hybrid campaign in the UK.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: The intelligence chief said there had been 50 arrests in the last year over Iran-linked activities.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: Much of this Iranian aggression has been aimed at Jewish communities, Sir Ken added, and also at "harder targets, like military sites".
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: Sir Ken did not mention arrests at RAF Fairford directly during his speech, but told reporters afterwards the incident was "not unique".
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: He added: "We have seen Iranian interest beyond RAF Fairford in the UK." The incident at the airbase in Gloucesteshire, where three suspicious vans were seen parked nearby, has seen seven people arrested and bailed by counter-terrorism police.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: Burnham has said the incident was "almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard".
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: On the emerging threat posed by AI, Sir Ken said: "It can produce propaganda and radicalising material tailored to the individual.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: "We've caught terrorists seeking to exploit Al to improve their reconnaissance and attack methodologies, with Al-enabled drones adding a new twist." Sir Ken said the bioweapons threat posed by AI was "not yet realised" but warned the technology has the "potential to change the stakes".
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: The UK Intelligence Community - MI5, GCHQ, MI6 - is working closely with the UK's globally respected AI Security Institute to take them on." Sir Ken said AI poses unknown threats, telling Thames House: "Put at its simplest, human history has given us no experience of facing an actor which is smarter than we are".
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: He announced MI5 had launched an AI Threat Assessment Centre, which he said would assess sources and "separate the bluster from the realities".
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: In April, the UK's terrorism threat level was raised to severe for the first time in five years, meaning an attack is highly likely.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: Sir Ken said Islamist groups like Al Qaeda and so-called Islamic State both continue to direct and inspire attacks, while the increased risk was also driven "in significant part" by extreme right-wing terrorism.
sentences.article_title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI

sentences.text: He said: "That investigation generated insight that enabled one of our international partners to prevent a lethal attack on their soil." China funding UK research and sending it to Beijing's spies, MI5 warns MI5 accepts it gave evidence based on lies in neo-Nazi spy case

sentences.text: Countries around the world have had their future economic prospects assessed by  influential body, the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
sentences.article_title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF

sentences.text: What the IMF says matters – it aims to keep the global economy stable and its twice-yearly forecasts are one of the most authoritative looks at what is really going on around the world.
sentences.article_title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF

sentences.text: Yet like all forecasts they can also turn out to be incorrect, so they shouldn't be treated as gospel.
sentences.article_title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF

sentences.text: Here are three things we've learnt about the UK from the IMF's latest report.
sentences.article_title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF

sentences.text: The global economy has been rocked by the US-Israel war with Iran.
sentences.article_title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF

sentences.text: The transportation and production of energy in the Middle East has been severely disrupted, causing oil prices to jump and inflation to rise.
sentences.article_title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF

sentences.text: To calm the rate of price rises, central banks, including the Bank of England, are expected to hike interest rates in the coming months.
sentences.article_title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF

sentences.text: Despite all this, the IMF said the global economy is doing much better than expected, partly because of the surge of investment into artificial intelligence (AI).
sentences.article_title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF

sentences.text: And this is good news for the UK.
sentences.article_title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF

sentences.text: The IMF said its economy would expand by 1.3% in 2026, up from the 1% it predicted in July, before slowing in 2027.
sentences.article_title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF

sentences.text: A growing economy means companies are investing more and hiring more people while shoppers have more money to spend.
sentences.article_title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF

sentences.text: A shrinking economy means the reverse is true.
sentences.article_title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF

sentences.text: There is increased concern about how much money countries are borrowing, but the IMF said the UK is doing better than all other major economies at this.
sentences.article_title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF

sentences.text: The IMF said the UK "basically stands out, along with India" when it comes to addressing the problem and by 2031 it is projected to have the lowest annual borrowing of the G7 group of countries, which includes Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the US.
sentences.article_title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF

sentences.text: Sir Howard Davies, former deputy governor of the Bank of England, said this was largely because the UK has a government with a majority which has committed to tackling the situation, which it is expected to achieve either through tax rises, cuts to public services, or a mix of both.
sentences.article_title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF

sentences.text: The Brexit debate is back.

sentences.text: For years, it felt like the only thing Westminster talked about.

sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Why the prime minister wants to talk about Brexit again

sentences.text: This video can not be played Burnham: Post-Brexit status quo with Europe 'not good enough for Britain' With the arrival of Andy Burnham as prime minister, that has changed, despite what he said just a few months before he arrived in Downing Street.

sentences.text: Americans head to the polls on 3 November to decide how the rest of Donald Trump's presidency will play out.
sentences.article_title: Where the US midterm elections will be won and lost

sentences.text: Thousands of races are taking place across the US, at different levels of government.
sentences.article_title: Where the US midterm elections will be won and lost

sentences.text: But the main event for voters will be electing members of the House of Representatives and the Senate, the two chambers that make up Congress.
sentences.article_title: Where the US midterm elections will be won and lost

sentences.text: Both of them are currently controlled by the Republicans, the president's party.
sentences.article_title: Where the US midterm elections will be won and lost

sentences.text: The success or failure of Trump's final two years in office could rest on the outcome.

sentences.text: Here's our visual guide to where the battle for power will be won and lost - from approval ratings, to key races and issues and the huge amount of money being spent.

sentences.text: One of the reasons the opposition Democrats have a chance to take back Congress is the president's low approval rating, which is a good indicator for how well his party could perform.
sentences.article_title: Where the US midterm elections will be won and lost

sentences.text: He began his second term as president with an approval rating of just over 50%, according to polling resource website Silver Bulletin, but it quickly fell into the 40s.
sentences.article_title: Where the US midterm elections will be won and lost

sentences.text: It was hovering around 42% when Trump decided to launch air strikes with Israel against Iran at the end of February this year but it fell below 40% shortly afterwards.
sentences.article_title: Where the US midterm elections will be won and lost

sentences.text: It is currently sitting at about 37%.
sentences.article_title: Where the US midterm elections will be won and lost

sentences.text: Eight years ago, Trump's approval rating was significantly higher at this point in his first term, at 43%.
sentences.article_title: Where the US midterm elections will be won and lost

sentences.text: Joe Biden's at the same point in his term was at 40%.
sentences.article_title: Where the US midterm elections will be won and lost

sentences.text: In both cases, the sitting president lost control of the House in the midterms but kept hold of the Senate.
sentences.article_title: Where the US midterm elections will be won and lost

sentences.text: But Trump's poor ratings help explain why Democrats are hopeful of winning both chambers of Congress and why they are setting their sights on states that Republicans have won consistently in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Where the US midterm elections will be won and lost

sentences.text: The current Republican majority in the House of Representatives, the lower chamber, is as thin as it gets - they have 218 representatives, which is the exact number needed to have control, plus one independent who votes with them.

sentences.article_title: Where the US midterm elections will be won and lost

sentences.text: And on Tuesday, five justices at the UK's highest court were asked to consider whether Field could have made Mr Farquhar cause his own death without Field legally being responsible.

sentences.text: During his murder trial prosecutors said Field drove Farquhar to believe he was losing his mind, secretly drugging him and spiking his whisky so his death would appear to be suicide or an accident, allowing Field to inherit his home and money.

sentences.article_title: Supreme Court hears church warden murder appeal

sentences.text: He received a concurrent 16-year sentence for those offences.
sentences.article_title: Supreme Court hears church warden murder appeal

sentences.text: He was cleared of conspiring or attempting to murder Moore-Martin and of possessing an article for use in fraud.

sentences.text: Benjamin Field was jailed in 2019 after being convicted of murdering Peter Farquhar David Perry KC, for the CPS, said Field would not be legally responsible only if Farquhar had agreed to Field's plan knowing it was intended to kill him.
sentences.article_title: Supreme Court hears church warden murder appeal

sentences.text: Perry told the Supreme Court Field had "set out cynically to seduce Mr Farquhar" even though Field was heterosexual and "covertly" put medication - including the sedative Dalmane and hallucinogenic drugs - into his food or drink.

sentences.text: The barrister said that if any substance was covertly administered, or if Farquhar was misled about what he was drinking prior to his death, there would be "no dispute" that Field is guilty of murder.

sentences.text: "It must follow that if Ben Field, possessed of a continuous intent to kill over many years, had handed Peter Farquhar his car keys at his request, and Peter Farquhar had driven off and died in a traffic accident, then Ben Field would have caused Peter Farquhar's death and been guilty of murder," he said.
sentences.article_title: Supreme Court hears church warden murder appeal

sentences.text: Men were seen leaving HMP Durham About 650 more offenders are leaving jails in England and Wales on Tuesday, in the second phase of the early release scheme - the government's plan to tackle the prison population crisis.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: It includes offenders sentenced to up to two and a half years who are leaving jail after serving a third of their sentence behind bars, rather than half.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: The second wave of releases comes as the government takes its plan to radically overhaul criminal courts back to Parliament - but also as probation officers prepare to vote in a ballot that could lead to a strike over pay and workload.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: Some 700 offenders left jail early on 1 October - all of whom were serving terms of less than 19 months.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: Tuesday's second stage begins the process of releasing batches of offenders on increasingly longer sentences - culminating next June with those serving more than 12 years.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: Around 5,000 prisoners are scheduled to be released, down from 6,000 after ministers intervened to make rapists and the most serious child sex offenders exempt.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: Prisoners convicted of manslaughter are also excluded, meaning the killers of PC Andrew Harper, who died in the line of duty in 2019, will not be eligible.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: Those jailed for a range of offences, including members of child grooming gangs convicted of indecent assault are also ineligible.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said "the programme is clearly not working," stating she is "worried about dangerous people being let out on the street when they haven't served their sentence, haven't been rehabilitated".
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: Victims' groups have also raised concerns about the scheme.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: Alice Russell-Harris from the charity Refuge - which supports survivors of domestic abuse - told the BBC that domestic abuse perpetrators are among those being released.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: Reports of failures in the electronic tagging system have added to their concerns.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: The scheme is "dangerous and should not go ahead," Oakeshott told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: A released prisoner is greeted by a friend as he leaves HMP Wandsworth prison in south London as part of the early release scheme Typically, those being released should expect to be electronically tagged and subject to other monitoring conditions for the second third of their sentence.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: But the probation service union, Napo, said the releases put enormous strain on its members, who monitor offenders in the community.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: Probation officers are "absolutely overwhelmed with work," Napo's general secretary Ian Lawrence told the BBC, saying those being released require "intensive supervision" and "the sheer weight of numbers causes pressure".
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: "None of our people go to work to see people injured, hurt, or for reoffending to happen," he said, but the numbers coming out means the probation service need more resources.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: There are also concerns over delays in fitting electronic tags, which are used by probation officers to track curfews and conditions of a court or prison order.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: A report by His Majesty's Inspectorate of Probation (HMIP) found that almost half of the tags used to track offenders are not fitted on time, with some criminals waiting up to five months.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: Official data which will show if there has been any improvement to electronic tagging will not be released for several months.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: On Tuesday, the union's members will meet to discuss next week's vote, which could lead to strike action.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: Probation officers have been offered a 5% pay rise by the Ministry of Justice (MoJ), while it had demanded 12% as part of a plan to make up for loss of earnings caused by cuts from 2010.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: The MoJ says the offer is fair and has been accepted by two other unions and is twinned with a £700m investment in probation to recruit 1,300 extra officers and the roll-out of AI tools to cut the workload of monitoring offenders.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: Several people were released under the first tranche of the scheme are already back behind bars.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: Eight men were arrested by Greater Manchester Police (GMP) days after leaving prison under the government's early release scheme.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: Five were arrested for breaches of criminal orders, including a domestic abuse prevention order, and others were held on suspicion of robbery, drug offences and domestic violence, GMP said.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: While the second phase of prison releases gets under way, the government is bringing its criminal court reform plan back before MPs, after announcing a week ago that it had abandoned the most controversial element of it.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: The revised plan drops proposals for a new form of Crown Court where a judge alone, sitting without a jury of ordinary people, would reach a verdict against suspects facing up to three years in prison.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: However, jury trials will still be scrapped for the most complex and long fraud cases - and another 5,500 trials will be kept in the lower magistrates court by ending a defendant's right to ask for a jury trial.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: The government says it will expand the use of so-called "blitz" or "short trial" courts after pilots have shown that grouping similar cases together can speed up their progression through the courts - cutting backlogs.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: One of the pilots at the Old Bailey led to the London backlog of 500 cases concerning assaults on emergency workers being cut in half over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: A major review of criminal courts by former appeal judge Sir Brian Leveson recommended more virtual hearings for defendants to slash wasted time bringing them to and from cells.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: The government has now ordered pilots for defendants to appear direct from police cells.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: On Monday, the government announced it had accepted more than 150 of his 180 recommendations to modernise the criminal courts.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: It has rejected his advice to retain a restriction on volunteer magistrates that means they can only jail an offender for 12 months.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: Under the government's plan magistrates will have the power to jail for up to two years - the aim being to keep more cases out of Crown Court, to help clear backlogs.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme

sentences.text: Ronald Dowling was driving his Maserati Ghibli carelessy in poor weather conditions when the crash happened in October 2023 A Maserati driver who killed a woman and seriously injured two others has been given a suspended prison sentence.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: Ronald Dowling, 66, overtook a vehicle in heavy rain before aquaplaning, skidding across the carriageway and hitting Sharon Berry's car in the fatal crash at New Inn, Pontypool, on 26 October 2023.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: His wife, Kim Dowling, was left paralysed, and passenger Jane Beedell also suffered extensive injuries.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: Dowling, who previously pleaded guilty to causing death and serious injury by careless driving, was sentenced to 27 months in prison, suspended for two years.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: Despite wet and windy conditions, heavy rain and high levels of surface water, he was travelling at 76mph (122 km/h) just three seconds before the crash.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: After aquaplaning, the defendant crashed into a stationary black Audi A3 driven by Sharon, who had pulled over because of the weather conditions.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: She suffered catastrophic injuries and spent three months in hospital before her death in January 2024.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: In a victim impact statement, her son Luke Berry, who is expecting a child, described the family's loss as immeasurable, saying his mother would never get the chance to meet her grandchild.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: He said: "She was loving, caring and would do anything to make sure I was OK.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: "My family will never be the same without her." The court was also told Jane Beedell suffered multiple injuries in the crash, including chest and elbow injuries, bruising, wounds to her fingers, bleeding on the brain and multiple fractures to her ribs.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: She was placed in an induced coma for weeks, and told the court the crash had left her struggling with "fear, anxiety and depression".
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: "I used to be confident, strong and an outgoing individual," she said, explaining how she now relies on family and friends for daily support and struggles with everyday tasks, finding it difficult to go out alone.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: After 48 years working in the civil service, Jane said she had lost her job and now relied on benefits.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: She said she was devastated by the changes to her life, adding: "I sometimes feel guilty I survived".
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: The court heard how Kim Dowling was left paralysed with a broken back and neck and unable to speak after her voice box was removed following the crash.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: Mitigating, Dowling's barrister said the defendant felt "deep regret and remorse for the loss of life", along with "strong feelings of guilt and emotional distress".
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: The court heard that every time Dowling looked at his wife, he was reminded of what he had done.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: The case was initially brought as dangerous driving, but the charges were later changed to careless driving, to which he pleaded guilty.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: Dowling had previously been disqualified from driving for six months about 15 years ago after reaching 12 penalty points, the court heard.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: However, he had no previous convictions despite years of long-distance driving for work and was described as a man of "good character" who was a full-time carer for his wife.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: During the sentencing, Judge Hughes said Sharon Berry had suffered a "senseless death", adding that "no amount of sentence given to Dowling would bring her back".
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: Dowling was sentenced to 27 months in prison for causing death by careless driving and two counts of causing serious injury by careless driving, suspended for two years.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: He was also disqualified from driving for four years, ordered to complete 250 hours of unpaid community work and pay £1,630 in prosecution costs.
sentences.article_title: Maserati driver given suspended sentence after killing woman in crash

sentences.text: The Where Is My Husband! singer revealed there were 1.8 million sign-ups for her one-off 5,000-seat performance at the Royal Albert Hall on 23 October.
sentences.article_title: Raye hits back at ticket touts who 'overwhelmed' sign-up for Albert Hall show

sentences.text: To avoid a pre-sale which she felt scalpers could exploit, Raye said the sign-up list had been manually reviewed to identify a shortlist of people believed to be "real fans".
sentences.article_title: Raye hits back at ticket touts who 'overwhelmed' sign-up for Albert Hall show

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the Royal Albert Hall said they "invest heavily" in protecting their ticketing systems from "automated attacks" but the "law needs to catch up".
sentences.article_title: Raye hits back at ticket touts who 'overwhelmed' sign-up for Albert Hall show

sentences.text: The award-winning artist said she had "never witnessed bots on this scale" and was changing the process as it is "so important" to her that fans can buy tickets at the face value price.
sentences.article_title: Raye hits back at ticket touts who 'overwhelmed' sign-up for Albert Hall show

sentences.text: "I'm not sure what the future holds for ticketing, I do know this experience has really opened my eyes," she said in a statement shared on her social media accounts , external .

sentences.text: "Me and my team are going to think really hard about what we can do in the future." Raye said the fans manually selected would receive a pre-sale link and code by email at 11:45 BST on Tuesday, and pre-sale opened shortly afterwards.

sentences.text: Heating oil customers facing soaring bills have been promised better regulation of the sector by the government.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: Ministers say they will tighten up rules, promote competition and give customers clearer compensation routes if things go wrong.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: Minimum order levels, set for some customers, will be reviewed.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: With prices close to having doubled in the past year, some campaigners have called for heating oil customers to benefit from the same cap as regular, variable gas and electricity tariffs in England, Scotland and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: But there is no sign of the government proposing such a change, nor when the stricter rules will take effect.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: Ministers said they would work with industry to "develop a regulatory regime for the heating oil market, protecting consumers and promoting competition".
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: In the meantime, oil users have been offered discounts on heat pumps, a code of practice is in place, and industry practices setting minimum order volumes at 500 litres for some consumers will be reviewed.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: Domestic tanks typically hold between 1,000 and 2,000 litres.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: The government said this had left some people having to pay for more heating oil than they might need.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: Buy now or wait and hope?
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: Families face gamble on heating oil Prices have soared since the start of the US-Israeli war with Iran.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: In March, the government announced a support package worth £53m for low-income families who use heating oil.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: The funding is distributed by local authorities, which set their own criteria for eligibility.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: A subsequent inquiry by the UK's competition watchdog, the Competition and Markets Authority, found that 1,700 households were forced to "re-order at significantly higher prices or go without fuel" after the war broke out, costing them up to £350.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: But those whose orders were cancelled and prices raised were told they were entitled to compensation.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: The government has now announced it will accept the CMA's recommendation to strengthen regulation in the sector.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: Energy minister Polly Billington said: "Thousands of heating oil customers felt they had nowhere to turn when they paid the price of rising oil and gas costs earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: Energy is an essential good and people should not have to think twice about whether they're protected in the market.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: That's why we will reform the sector." Nick says heating his home now feels more like an investment than a regular household bill Nick, a heating oil customer from West Suffolk, told the BBC's Your Voice that "off-grid households remain a major policy blind spot" for the government.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: "Any protection from UK government for domestic heating oil users will be very welcome, providing this is for all domestic heating oil users," the 28-year-old said.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: He rents a three-bedroom home with his partner.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: He said they had seen prices more than double in a year, to quotes of 111p per litre.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: "Heating my home is now no longer another household bill, but almost an investment," he said.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: He called on tax cuts for customers, or the extension of the price cap to heating oil - a demand also made by charity National Energy Action.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: Tim Buckman, chief executive of price comparison site Boiler Juice, told the BBC he wants stronger protections for consumers but the main problem was that heating oil is twice as expensive as it was before the war.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: "Just putting regulation in place is not going to reduce the price for customers.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: What we would like to see is the VAT off heating oil or targeting that specifically." Some 1.5 million households depend on heating oil, but they do not have the same consumer protections as electricity and gas customers.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: However, energy regulator Ofgem, which sets the cap for standard variable tariffs, only covers England, Wales and Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: Most heating oil customers are in Northern Ireland, where 60% of households rely on it, but where regulation is separate.
sentences.article_title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise

sentences.text: It is likely Ofgem will regulate heating oil in England, Scotland and Wales, and the UK government said it would "engage with the Northern Ireland Executive as they consider these recommendations in parallel".

sentences.text: Cardiff Magistrates' Court hears that Joe Cordina was "set up" during a fight at a petrol station in February Former boxing world champion Joe Cordina was "retaliating" during a fight where he punched a man at a petrol station, a court has heard.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: Cordina is standing trial charged with assault by beating relating to an incident on 27 February involving Jamie O'Brien.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: Cardiff Magistrates' Court heard the altercation came to light days later after a video was published on WalesOnline, filmed by a witness at a Texaco garage in the Pentwyn area of Cardiff.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: O'Brien's sister told police her brother "hated" Cordina, the court was told, and she feared he had "sought" him out.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: A second assault by beating charge against Cordina was dropped on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: O'Brien previously admitted a charge of assault by beating .
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: CCTV footage of the incident "which took place over several minutes" was played to the court, showing Cordina filling up his car and walking over to O'Brien who stood on the pavement nearby.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: Prosecutor Alex Orndal said O'Brien "pushed Mr Cordina with his shoulder" and Cordina then "punched him with sufficient force to push him to the ground", where he then pushed him "repeatedly".
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: "Mr Cordina has initiated the confrontation," Orndal said, adding "Cordina was not protecting himself but retaliating".
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: There was then "aggression" from O'Brien, the court heard, as Cordina raised a golf club and O'Brien lunged at him, before a number of blows were exchanged.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: O'Brien was eventually restrained and "posed no further threat", the court heard, but Cordina threw a further punch at him.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: In a police interview on 11 March 2026 Cordina denied the charges against him and said he was being stared at by O'Brien, initially thinking he wanted a photo.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: The former world champion explained that "having been shoved, he felt threatened" and that "he punched him later out of instinct due to Mr O'Brien's actions", the court heard.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: He also told police that Jamie O'Brien threatened to stab him and said he would blow up his and his mother's houses.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: Cordina's defence barrister, Tom Crowther KC, told the court O'Brien had been identified by family members from the video circulating online, who had raised concerns about his behaviour.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: During the hearing Crowther asked investigating officer PC Samuel Penman to watch the video that had circulated online.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: He said it was plain to see that they were "watching and waiting" for Cordina, suggesting it was a set up.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: Penman said it was not obvious but he did agree that the person filming "seemingly started recording prior to any physical altercation going on".
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: The court heard that when O'Brien was arrested he "argued with officers" and "challenged" them.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: Penman admitted it was a "mistake" not to question O'Brien's sister about her concerns that her brother held a "vendetta" against Cordina.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: Cordina told the court that people recognised him "four or five times a day", which was generally positive with people shaking his hand or asking for a photo.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: But it was heard that a fortnight before the incident, the defendant had been told by police there was a threat to his life - something that left him shocked and "worried".
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: He denied knowing O'Brien, despite the suggestion they had boxed together at some point.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: Explaining why he hit O'Brien, he said: "It was just a reaction, I felt a bit threatened.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: I wasn't going over to seek any trouble - I was just defending myself." Asked why he pushed O'Brien down afterwards and repeatedly said "don't ever do that again", Cordina said he was protecting himself.
sentences.article_title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears

sentences.text: The court heard a number of character witness statements in support of Cordina, including from his agent Ian Bird and Llanrumney Phoenix boxing club who called him an "outstanding role model".

sentences.text: Retail chain Poundland is in talks with potential buyers as it seeks a rescue deal, it has confirmed.

sentences.article_title: Poundland in rescue talks as owners seek buyer

sentences.text: But a union representing shopworkers warned that the retailer could fall into administration if that deal falls through, putting thousands of jobs at risk.
sentences.article_title: Poundland in rescue talks as owners seek buyer

sentences.article_title: Poundland in rescue talks as owners seek buyer

sentences.article_title: Poundland in rescue talks as owners seek buyer

sentences.article_title: Poundland in rescue talks as owners seek buyer

sentences.text: The amount of time children in England spend on screens at school could be harming their "physical and developmental health", a group of more than 150 clinicians has warned.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: GPs, paediatricians and other specialists said in an open letter to Education Secretary Lucy Powell and Health Secretary Yvette Cooper that tablets and laptops are being used without a full understanding of their long-term health impacts, including on eye health.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The clinicians said they are prescribing glasses, hearing aids and speech therapy to children "for a problem that is unintentionally being made worse in our schools".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The government said it was consulting on screen time guidance for children aged five to 18 but that technology could be a powerful learning tool if used properly.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: The group of clinicians said nearly one million children are using screens in most lessons, despite studies suggesting a rise in short-sightedness.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: They pointed to an analysis of 276 studies covering 5.4 million participants around the world.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: That analysis, they claimed, found a rise in short-sightedness among children and adolescents from around 24% in 1990 to almost 36% by 2023, warning the condition is associated with an increased risk of a range of eye health problems.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: She told BBC Radio 4's Today programme parents had not been given the chance to "opt out" of the "excessive" use of screens in schools, which risks children "just not thriving" in education.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: She said an "explosion" in short-sightedness "cannot be put down to genetics alone".
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: It also warned that children with special educational needs are "disproportionately" directed to screen-based learning.
sentences.article_title: Cut screen time in classrooms to avoid long-term health issues, clinicians urge

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, said education technology can provide schools with "very effective learning tools".

sentences.text: Maternity unit staff were not told for more than a year that testing had revealed their workplace was breaching safety limits for nitrous oxide (file pic) NHS maternity staff who were exposed to excessive levels of nitrous oxide have received "landmark" payouts totalling £735,000, a union said.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: Basildon Hospital in Essex settled claims from 121 staff, including 85 midwives, who took legal action after reporting fatigue, anxiety, headaches and "brain fog" after the gas levels breached safety limits.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: The Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust said it had apologised to staff.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: The Royal College of Midwives (RCM) said it was the largest group legal action ever brought by midwives in the UK.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: The gas, also known as Entonox, is used to provide temporary pain relief for women giving birth.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: The staff members behind the claims were found to have breathed it in over long shifts for months and years.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: According to an internal report from Basildon Hospital, some members of staff were exposed to levels up to 30 times higher than the legal workplace exposure limit between 2021 and 2023.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: They were also not told for 16 months about test results commissioned by the trust that showed their exposure had breached safety thresholds.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: The legal action was first revealed by the BBC in May.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: The trust settled the claims after admitting its staff had been exposed to dangerously high levels of the gas.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: Gill Walton, from the RCM, said the settlement should "make every NHS employer sit up and take notice" NHS Resolution, which manages legal claims and compensation cases on behalf of the NHS in England, confirmed the payouts.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: A spokesman said: "We can confirm that 121 claims have been settled for a total of £735,000.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: Some other claims remain outstanding.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: We are unaware of any larger group of claims brought by midwives." One claim has yet to be settled according to the RCM.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: That delay is unacceptable," he added.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: The Mid and South Essex NHS Trust said it acknowledged that it should have acted faster Gill Walton, the RCM chief executive and general secretary, said: "For years, midwives at Basildon were breathing in nitrous oxide at dangerous levels while they cared for women and babies.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: "Even once the problem had been discovered, it was more than a year before staff were told.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: That is simply not acceptable and no midwife should ever be treated that way," she said.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: She continued: "This is a landmark settlement for our members and it should make every NHS employer sit up and take notice.
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: If you don't protect your staff - the RCM will hold you to account".
sentences.article_title: NHS staff get 'landmark' payout over gas exposure

sentences.text: The RCM has also written to every NHS trust in England to make them aware of the risks of the gas and said it had also "raised concerns about the trust's lack of action" with the Health and Safety Executive (HSE).

sentences.text: Political figures who are not currently MPs will be given police support, the home secretary has announced.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: Shabana Mahmood told MPs there was "insufficient protection" for those serving in public life and that the new announcement will cover peers, former MPs and party spokespeople.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: She also announced an urgent, independent review of security arrangements for high-profile figures including politicians and royals.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: It comes three months after Reform UK spokeswoman and former Conservative MP Ann Widdecombe was found dead at her home in Devon, having been hit on the head with a hammer 21 times as she ate lunch.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: Joshua Kerry, 28, has been charged with her murder, and he was also charged with preparing acts of terror against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: Kerry is alleged to have carried out research on prominent targets over a period of two years, including trying to gain entry into Farage's London home.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: Speaking in the Commons on Monday, Mahmood said that "robust debate and criticism are part of this job - threats, abuse and violence are not." She did not elaborate on what the support would involve, but told MPs it would include access to a named police officer and help with wider security measures.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: The safety of politicians has been a prominent issue in recent years, following the murders of Conservative MP Sir David Amess in 2021 and Labour MP Jo Cox in 2016.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: "We owe it to them and to everyone who believes in a fair and open country to ensure that those who serve at all levels receive the protection they deserve," Mahmood added.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: The "root and branch" independent review into security arrangements will be led by former national security advisor Stephen Lovegrove, and will look into "physical threats, online risks and the dangers posed within our more polarised society".
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: Mahmood confirmed that the review will report within six months, and build on the existing work of Sir Robert Buckland, who is leading a separate review into the murder of Sir David.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: In response, shadow home secretary Chris Philp welcomed the extension of protective measures, saying threats to elected representatives are threats to democracy.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: Decisions over the security of current MPs and members of the House of Lords are made by the House of Parliament's security team.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: There is a separate, independent committee, the Royal and VIP Executive Committee (Ravec), to deal with high-profile political candidates, which is staffed by officials from the Home Office, the Cabinet Office, and the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: The Jo Cox Foundation welcomed the home secretary's announcement but said "strengthening physical security" alone was not enough.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: "We must also tackle the root causes - including online harms and education - to prevent future attacks," its chief executive Olivia Field said in a statement on X.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: According to data released to the BBC in April , the number of alleged offences against MPs have increased year-on-year, with 976 recorded in 2025, compared to 364 in 2019.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: MPs reported 4,064 crimes to the Met's Parliamentary Liaison Team between 2019 and 2025.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: Most offences were related to malicious communications followed by harassment, and criminal damage to a building.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: In 2025, there were 50 death threats reported - up from 31 the previous year.
sentences.article_title: Government expands police support to political figures who are not MPs

sentences.text: Dr Allison Gardner, the Labour MP for Stoke-on-Trent South, is leading a group of MPs to improve recognition of chronic UTIs Warning: This story contains reference to suicide An MP says she was left "feeling like a drug user" while trying desperately to find pain relief for chronic urinary tract infections (UTIs).
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: Labour MP Dr Allison Gardner has been living with the "searing pain" of recurrent  infections for about 10 years, after first experiencing symptoms with perimenopause.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: According to the Chronic Urinary Tract Infection Campaign (CUTIC), more than 1.6 million women in the UK suffer from chronic lower urinary tract symptoms, but there is no official medical definition of the condition.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: That is something Gardner is trying to change, with the support of a cross party group of MPs in Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: Gardner told the BBC how a lack of consensus on what constituted a chronic UTI left her feeling sidelined by doctors, who did not always understand the condition and were limited in the length of antibiotic courses they could prescribe.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: "You end up hunting for a decent length of antibiotic courses that will give you some relief," she said.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: UTIs are caused by bacteria entering the urethra , external .
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: As women have a shorter urethra than men, bacteria are more likely to reach the bladder or kidneys and cause an infection.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: Chronic UTIs are infections where symptoms do not go away, and do not clear with a short course of antibiotics.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: They can also be difficult to diagnose, due to a lower level of bacteria shown in urine samples.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: Gardner told the BBC she had considered selling her home to pay for bladder removal surgery after years of pain "It's a searing pain every time you go to the loo" said Gardner, 60.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: "It's just like hot needles being inserted inside you and just burning, burning, burning." She told the BBC she had felt "gaslighted" by medics and had been told to "wipe yourself better" after describing intense pain.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: She was even told by one consultant to give up sex because it can cause a flare up.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: "You've got to fight all the time just to get treated sensibly and [not told] you've got anxiety, depression or are attention seeking," Gardner said.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: The pain and lack of answers about her condition eventually led her to a very dark place.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: "It got to the point where [I thought] 'if this is how my life is going to be,  I can't carry on'," she said.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: She was so desperate she even considered selling her house to pay for private surgery to have her bladder removed.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: It was around that time three years ago that she discovered Dr Cat Anderson, a Staffordshire-based GP who works in private practice and for the NHS.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: She was the first to identify that Gardner's symptoms were related to the menopause and prescribed her Hormone Replacement Therapy (HRT).
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: "I had two years free of UTI - I just had my life back," said Gardner.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: Asked whether going private went against her Labour principles that healthcare should be free, Gardner said: "You're stuck with a choice aren't you?
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: "You either suffer or you go private... so I don't judge." She added that she believed everyone should have access to the healthcare they needed.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: Anderson specialises in challenging UTI cases, and is leading a group of medical experts to develop a medical definition of chronic UTIs to differentiate it from other conditions.
sentences.article_title: Chronic UTIs made MP 'feel like a drug user'

sentences.text: This video can not be played Microsoft boss: 'If a company builds AI agents and they break loose, there should be a legal obligation to tell the victim' Milk and washing machines are currently more regulated than AI, the president of Microsoft has said.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: Brad Smith said there needed to be global safety rules in place, including a legal obligation to tell a "victim" if their system is breached by a rogue AI agent as well as deciding when outside evaluators should sign off on an AI product before it is released.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: His comments put him at odds with President Donald Trump, who said the sector should regulate itself so US firms don't lose out to Chinese rivals.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: But Smith said: "Right now, your washing machine is subject to more safety rules than AI.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: Every carton of milk that you see in the grocery store is subject to safety rules and inspection." Demands for laws and rules to control AI have grown after experts in the sector said they believed the technology is a threat to humanity.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: The bosses of the US-based AI giants such as Anthropic, OpenAI and Google DeepMind have all backed the idea of an AI development slowdown , but Trump has pushed against this.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: Speaking to the BBC's Big Boss Interview podcast, Smith called AI both a "tool and a weapon" that urgently needed to be regulated.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: "Let's get started today," he said.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: He said firms need "emergency brakes" – often known in the industry as 'kill switches' – to pause or slowdown AI if it got out of control in some way.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: He also said there should be a legal requirement for firms to write "incident reports" and tell victims if the technology goes rogue.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: He also suggested that independent government evaluators should vet new AI technology.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: "We know how to do this for other products," Smith said.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: "We should build on that knowledge and think about how to apply it to AI." Smith said the UK was best placed to drive forward these global rules for AI because of its AI Security Institute , external , launched during former prime minister Rishi Sunak's government as the AI Safety Institute.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: "In the world of technology, in the tech sector, most people that I know would say, if you ask them, name the country that is the leader in having this technical capability, they would say, it's very simple.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: They are the best." Smith's views are very different to those of his president, who believes the US should be going full-steam ahead on AI.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: Trump has repeatedly said that "whoever wins AI, wins".
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: However, Smith does not believe the US government would be as opposed to UK-led AI regulations as Trump's comments make it seem, suggesting the US would be more accepting of the UK making standards than the EU.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: "In Washington DC, people don't look at the UK and they don't look at London the way they look at Brussels – that's a strength," he said.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: "When you look at AI agents that have escaped human control, when you look at models that are so powerful that they're putting the world's cybersecurity at risk.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: I would say: The moment has arrived.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: "Let's speak calmly, maybe even softly, but firmly, and start to bring people together.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: I hope that's the role we can play as a company.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: I hope that's the role the UK can play as a country." Big Boss Interview: Microsoft's Brad Smith The president of the tech giant calls for global rules on AI, and says the UK is in the "best position" to lead the charge.
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: At the end of last month, Trump hosted the leaders of US tech giants OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, SpaceX, Meta, and Google at the White House where the executives signed a "morally binding" document .

sentences.text: The companies agreed to work with "independent auditors" to assess whether their AI systems are working as intended and make sure they do not "hack or access technical systems in unintended ways".
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: Smith said he applauds the statement and Microsoft is "happy to sign it".
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president

sentences.text: "It's a good step, it's a necessary step...
sentences.article_title: AI is less regulated than milk, says Microsoft president
