sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: A second head teachers' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections in England, saying it is "increasingly concerned about the welfare and morale" of its members.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: The Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL) also raised the prospect of potential strike action, saying a new grading system had become an "overbearing mess".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: On Friday, Ofsted's chief inspector Sir Martyn Oliver said an independent survey of education providers showed it was "on the right track" with inspections.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: The Department for Education (DfE) said ministers were "working with Ofsted and school leaders to ensure accountability is fair, proportionate and focused on helping every school get better".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: ASCL's announcement comes after another union, the National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) , said changes Ofsted made to inspections just under a year ago had been severely harmful to school leaders' welfare.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: ASCL said it had passed a motion of no confidence in "the ability of Ofsted's leadership to address the damage being done by the new inspection system", adding that it was "increasingly concerned about the welfare and morale of members".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary, said the union did not take the step "lightly", but added Ofsted's "warm words about recognising wellbeing pressures... have not been matched by the action necessary" and that "negotiation [had] hit a brick wall".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: "The current system is not fit for purpose.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: It is an overbearing mess and urgently needs to be reviewed," he said.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: Why the shake-up of school inspections risks causing new problems What is Ofsted and how does the new school ratings system work?
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: ASCL called on the government to pause inspections and review the system, and said it would survey members on whether to hold an informal ballot on industrial action if there was no change.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: In response, Ofsted said it had "worked hard to reduce the pressure of inspection in recent years, but we know workload and wellbeing remain a challenge".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: "We are working with the Department for Education on this and we will keep listening to feedback from professionals as we continue to improve what we do," a spokesperson added.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: England's schools inspectorate introduced the report card system to replace its previous one or two-word judgements last November, following the death of head teacher Ruth Perry, who took her own life after Ofsted downgraded her school from "outstanding" to "inadequate".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: An inquest ruled that an Ofsted inspection had contributed to her death in January 2023.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: That led to a change in how Ofsted assessed schools, bringing in report cards designed to grade schools on several areas, rather than focusing on one overall grade.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: An example of a new Ofsted inspection report Last month, the NAHT said testimonies from its members, seen by the BBC, suggested some school leaders had faced "intolerable" pressure because of the new inspections, leaving them "overwhelmed" and "anxious".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: It warned the system could pose a "risk to life" if changes were not forthcoming.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: An independent report, commissioned by Ofsted to evaluate its new framework, concluded this week that leaders were "generally positive" about their inspection experience, and that it was "more collaborative and accounts for context better than previous inspections".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: But it also said nearly half (48%) of school leaders who responded to its survey said their staff's mental wellbeing had been negatively affected "a fair amount" or "a lot" by a recent inspection.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: The interim report was based on focus groups and nearly 700 responses from school, college and early years leaders who were invited to complete a survey following inspections this year.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: A full report is due to be published next year.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: "I know that workload and wellbeing in education continue to be challenging, and I don't take that lightly.

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It will also let them decide on privacy settings for their account.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In a blog post, WhatsApp, clarified parents would not be given the power to see the messages their teen is sending and receiving, which along with calls would stay private and protected by end-to-end encryption.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it." The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: According to the firm, parents will be able to adjust or switch off the controls at any time.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The settings will be "straightforward to set up" using a Pin set by a parent, which teens will need if they want to switch off the controls.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Some of the new privacy tools include selecting who can see a child's profile photo and who can add them to groups.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Parents can also choose how their teenager uses Channels, which allows organisations and public figures to send out content.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And they will have the option of choosing between the default 13+ setting for Meta AI, the app's optional built-in AI assistant, or a stricter "Limited Content" option.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "All of these controls are being designed to support open conversations about how to use WhatsApp between parents and teens, while keeping everyone's personal messages private," the company said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The changes come as pressure mounts on tech companies from governments and regulators to change the way they operate in order to better protect children using their platforms.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In June, the government announced it plans to ban under-16s from social media platforms, with the restrictions expected to come into force in March 2027.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It said "highly effective age assurance" measures would be used to check the age of those using social media.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: WhatsApp is currently excluded from the ban because the government considers it a messaging service.

sentences.text: Cases of antisemitism affecting university students and staff in the UK increased in the last academic year, according to a charity that monitors antisemitic incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The Community Security Trust (CST) said it had recorded 95 "university-related" incidents in the 2025-26 academic year - up from 83 the year before.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said the number had fallen from its peak in the year after Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023 and the war in Gaza began, but remains "substantially higher" than before that point.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Universities UK (UUK) represents more than 140 institutions and said its members needed to "protect Jewish students and staff", adding that the findings were a "serious concern".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Lucy Powell, education secretary in England, said the findings in the CST report were "deeply troubling".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: "We expect universities to take a zero-tolerance approach to antisemitism, and are providing training to help university staff identify and respond to incidents swiftly," she said.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The CST defines an antisemitic incident as "university-related" if it concerns a student, member of staff or academic at a UK university "in their academic or student capacity" - including on campus and online.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: In 2022-23, the last academic year before the 7 October attack, the CST recorded 53 incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: That grew to 272 in 2023-24.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: A report from the charity examining the past two academic years says reported incidents fell in 2024-25 and but grew again in 2025-26.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The most common type of incident recorded by CST over both years was abusive behaviour, including verbal abuse, comments made in person or online and antisemitic graffiti.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Its report said that, for the first time, there were two occurrences of extreme violence in 2024-25.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said there were six reported assaults across both years, eight incidents of damage and desecration to Jewish property - five of which were in student accommodation - and ten threats.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Around two-thirds of reported incidents involved antisemitic language or targeting alongside references to Israel, Gaza, Hamas, the 7 October attack, and the subsequent conflicts in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The war in Gaza was triggered by the Hamas attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken hostage.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Israel launched a mass military offensive on Gaza in response which has killed around 74,000 people, according to the Hamas-run health ministry.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: He added that universities had "a duty to ensure that Jewish students and staff can study, work and participate on campus the same as anyone else".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Raphi Leon, president of the Union of Jewish Students, said the report "must be a shot in the arm to boost action to support Jewish students and tackle antisemitism".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Vivienne Stern, chief executive of UUK, said: "The rise in antisemitic incidents in the UK, including on university campuses, is a serious concern.

sentences.text: The largest teaching union had objected to the prospect of partly funding a 3.5% pay increase this year out of existing school budgets Schools in England are to get around £500 million in extra funding towards the teachers' pay award this school year, reducing the risk of a strike ballot by the largest education union.

sentences.text: England's biggest school leaders' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections, saying they could pose a "risk to life" for school staff.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) said the change to inspections, rolled out nationally just under a year ago, had been severely harmful to school leaders' welfare.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: It said schools should instead be rated using short narrative reports that set out their strengths and areas they could improve.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted said it had worked closely with unions and parents to develop the new report card inspection system and that it would continue to grade schools.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Ofsted, England's schools inspectorate, introduced the report card system to replace its previous one or two-word judgements last November, following the death of head teacher Ruth Perry , who took her own life after Ofsted downgraded her school from "outstanding" to "inadequate".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An inquest ruled that an Ofsted inspection had contributed to her death in January 2023.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: That led to a change in how Ofsted assessed schools, bringing in report cards designed to grade schools on several areas, rather than focusing on one overall grade.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: An example of a new Ofsted inspection report But the new system has faced criticism since it was first proposed , with Perry's sister Prof Julia Waters saying it appeared to be "a rehash of the discredited and dangerous system it is meant to replace".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The NAHT issued a claim in the High Court for a judicial review over the changes, arguing there had not been adequate consultation on the new report cards before they were introduced, but this was rejected.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Nearly a year after it was fully rolled out, the NAHT said evidence from its members suggested the new system is having a detrimental impact on school leaders' mental health.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Testimonies seen by the BBC suggest head teachers are being left "overwhelmed" and "anxious", with the pressure caused by the inspections described as "intolerable".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Although the system had been changed with the intention of lowering the burden on school leaders, the testimonies say the inspection and assessment process had become "higher stakes than ever before".
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Amanda Hulme, head teacher at Claypool Primary School in Bolton, said a recent inspection at her school had been "easily the most stressful experience" of her career.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "It was definitely damaging to my health and really quite distressing," she said.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "I couldn't sleep and it led to my blood pressure and pulse rate increasing.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Powell told LBC earlier this month that she took head teacher wellbeing "incredibly seriously" and that the system of accountability needed to be "supportive and understanding.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "I'll continue the work that I do with head teachers, head teacher representatives and others to make sure that we get this Ofsted framework, but also the culture and the whole regime, right," she said.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The NAHT said the results of a recent survey of its members suggested that the majority who responded felt that inspections had worsened in the past 12 months.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: The union is now calling for inspections to pause to allow for a "fundamental review of how inspection works", drawing on examples from other nations.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: In Wales, the inspectorate Estyn has removed judgements such as "excellent" and "good" from its reports, instead summarising findings by highlighting a school's strengths and areas for improvement.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Northern Ireland's Education and Training Inspectorate (ETI) also uses narrative reports without grades.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: Scotland's His Majesty's Inspectorate of Education (HIME) does use grades, but there has been a recent consultation on their use.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: NAHT general secretary Paul Whiteman said: "The clear theme emerging across all the feedback we have received is that this Ofsted framework is even more stressful than the one that preceded it.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "Ofsted exists to raise standards for children and to provide clear reporting to parents," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Union calls for halt to graded Ofsted inspections over health concerns

sentences.text: "We will continue to engage closely with trades unions – but we will also continue to grade schools." Have you been impacted by the issues discussed in this story?

sentences.text: The 21-year-old, from Netherlee in East Renfrewshire, has Rett Syndrome, a genetic neurological disorder which leaves her unable to speak or move and comes with a range of health problems including epilepsy.
sentences.article_title: Student who spells by blinking is denied chance to sit exam

sentences.text: For years, people with the condition were assumed to have profound learning disabilities but Romi, who uses special eye-gaze technology to communicate, is hoping to challenge that belief.
sentences.article_title: Student who spells by blinking is denied chance to sit exam

sentences.text: After months of work, she completed the coursework for National 4 (Nat 4) history and achieved a qualification last year.

sentences.article_title: Student who spells by blinking is denied chance to sit exam

sentences.text: But her hopes have been dashed by Scotland's exams body Qualifications Scotland (QS) which has rejected her family's requests for the adjustments Romi would need.
sentences.article_title: Student who spells by blinking is denied chance to sit exam

sentences.text: Romi told the BBC she deserved the same chance as everyone else About 18 months before exam time, her college and parents began discussions with QS, asking if she could sit it one question at a time over a number of weeks or potentially months.

sentences.article_title: Student who spells by blinking is denied chance to sit exam

sentences.text: Her parents also asked if she could use a "bank" of pre-agreed relevant words that would mean she would not have to spell out every letter.
sentences.article_title: Student who spells by blinking is denied chance to sit exam

sentences.text: Qualifications Scotland (QS) said no despite two children using eye gaze technology to sit GCSE exams in England earlier this year .

sentences.text: Romi's mum Gael said her daughter was starting with an incredible disadvantage Qualifications Scotland suggested Romi sit the exam all in one go, but her mum said that would be impossible because communicating using her eyes is so exhausting.

sentences.article_title: Student who spells by blinking is denied chance to sit exam

sentences.article_title: Student who spells by blinking is denied chance to sit exam

sentences.text: Ruth Lue-Quee is a mother and early years specialist who says parents should not be blamed for delays in their children's development For some parents the countdown to starting school means buying uniforms, labelling water bottles and trying to squeeze in one last summer holiday.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: For others there is a more basic question to tackle: can their child use the toilet on their own?
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: According to a survey by the charity Kindred Squared, almost a third of children starting school in the West Midlands last year were not fully toilet-trained and 42% of those arriving in reception were deemed not school-ready by primary school staff.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: This week the charity announced its potty-training scheme, which provides resources and support including increased training for nurseries, schools and professionals, will be rolled out in Solihull.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: In a pilot in York, which began in April, parents were sent potty-training and school readiness guides with their offers of a school place.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: Workshops were held, resources distributed and support offered through GPs, pharmacies, libraries and community hubs.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: As a result, the number of non-toilet-trained children starting reception fell by almost half.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: An early years specialist based in Wolverhampton has said the conversation about school readiness needs to extend well beyond the toilet.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: Ruth Lue-Quee, a former deputy head teacher and founder of My Mummy Teacher, works with parents and schools to support children's development through play-based learning.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: She said: "We want to be setting the foundations.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: Can they talk and have conversations?
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: Are you reading stories to them?
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: Are they moving their bodies?
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: Because all of those things are what then underpin the skills to be able to learn, practising everyday independence.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: Can they hang their coat or can they take their socks off?" But she warned that school readiness could become a source of anxiety for families and said it was important to recognise that children reached milestones at different speeds.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: "We need to be careful that school readiness doesn't become a checklist that four-year-olds are expected to pass or something that leaves parents feeling they have failed if their child develops differently," she said.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: "Childhood isn't a race." Lue-Quee believes there is more to school readiness than just toileting Rachel, a mother-of-two from Nottinghamshire, is one of Lue-Quee's clients.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: She tried to toilet-train her son when he was three but he had problems with withholding stools.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: She works as a teacher but said being on the other side of the problem as a parent was very different.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: "I'd say as a teacher, I feel I'm quite an informed parent in this area," she said.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: "So I was thinking, 'I know what's going on but I don't know what to do'.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: "It's not the parent, it's not being lazy; it's hard and it's a lot of effort," she added.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: She was told she would not be able to access funded support for her child until he was five, and it was not until the end of his reception year that the family received help.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: Now aged eight, her son is awaiting an assessment for ADHD, which Rachel believes could have affected aspects of his development despite going unnoticed in his early years.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: "Withholding can be trauma-informed and it can be because of passing something that has hurt at some point or someone has reacted badly to them having an accident," she said, adding she believed embarrassment and shame had contributed to her son's difficulties after he had an accident at nursery.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: Helen Davies, a health visitor and children's nurse based in Stafford, said children who repeatedly had accidents may be frightened of the toilet, leading to constipation.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: "A child who is struggling may be frightened of the toilet, withholding poo or experiencing constipation.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: Repeated accidents should prompt curiosity about what is getting in the way rather than an assumption that parents have not tried hard enough," she said.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: Helen Davies says problems with toileting could have underlying causes Annamaria Bailey, 37, a mother-of-two from Wolverhampton, said toilet-training her two-year-old involved taking four days off from her flexible work-from-home job as an independent travel agent.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: "I'm a stay-at-home mum," she said.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: "I don't know how I would block out four consecutive days of work." She said helping children with skills such as toileting and communication could be a particular challenge for families where both parents worked full time.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: "There's no longer that time to sit and play with your children now as much as you would like," she said.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: "I just genuinely don't think it's the parents' fault." Annamaria Bailey took time off work to potty-train her child Lue-Quee highlighted that older generations are working later too, meaning some families "don't have the village like they used to have".
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: Kindred Squared said the West Midlands had seen one of the biggest declines in school readiness in the country, with the number of children lacking skills such as toileting increasing year on year.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: Solihull Council said it had "had reports locally of a higher proportion of children arriving at school in nappies or pull-ups in comparison to a few years ago", adding that its new potty-training scheme would form part of its wider Best Start in Life programme.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: Bailey, a former reception teacher and early years lead, said she had worked in "deprived and affluent areas" and had seen inequalities in school readiness.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: "It comes down to income," she said.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: While some parents were able to buy parenting books, she said those on lower incomes had less access to information.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: "Books are quite expensive," she added, suggesting families could be given free toilet-training resources when their children turned two.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: Davies, who provides one-to-one guidance through her company Essential Parenting, said families may not be getting "timely, consistent support before difficulties become entrenched".
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: She said financial pressure, parental stress, limited opportunities for play and difficulty accessing early years provision and professional advice could make preparing for school harder.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: "Public services are essential, particularly for families who cannot afford private support," she said.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: For teachers, the issue is tangible.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: A reception teacher dealing with several children who need help with toileting has to balance that against the needs of the rest of the class.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: "It's really, really difficult for schools to be able to facilitate supporting that alongside teaching," said Lue-Quee.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: Schools are absolutely desperate for resources and are having to make the best decisions with the money they have.
sentences.article_title: Why are so many four-year-olds not potty-trained before school?

sentences.text: The ringed owls will be tracked to see how well nature-friendly farming is helping their numbers Barn owl chicks have been ringed in Purbeck for the first time to help track their movements and if the area's conservation-focused farming is working.

sentences.article_title: Owls ringed to measure benefits of wildlife farming

sentences.article_title: Owls ringed to measure benefits of wildlife farming

sentences.text: Red squirrel populations across Britain have dramatically declined Groups trying to protect red squirrels are being invited to bid for funding from a £250,000 pot.

sentences.text: The Red Squirrel Recovery Network (RSRN) said it hoped to "engage people from all  backgrounds" with grants of up to £500 available for smaller activities to £5,000 to support ideas with a wider reach.

sentences.text: The project, which started in 2025 , works with conservation partners and volunteer groups across Northumberland, Cumbria, Manchester, Lancashire, Merseyside and southern Scotland to raise awareness of the endangered species.
sentences.article_title: Red squirrel project opens £250k community grant

sentences.text: In May, animal welfare group Save Our Reds said the species "still clings on" across Cumbria, Northumberland and the North Pennines but could disappear within 25 years.
sentences.article_title: Red squirrel project opens £250k community grant

sentences.text: Red squirrel populations across Britain have dramatically declined and have been estimated at about 287,000, the RSRN said.
sentences.article_title: Red squirrel project opens £250k community grant

sentences.text: According to Natural England , external , causes for the decline include the introduction of grey squirrels from the USA and Canada from 1876 spreading the squirrelpox virus, which is fatal to the red squirrels only.

sentences.text: Save Our Reds said habitat loss and weak enforcement of existing protections were adding to the problem.
sentences.article_title: Red squirrel project opens £250k community grant

sentences.text: Dermot Gethings is vice chair of the Preston & District Astronomical Society Nearly 54 years ago, Apollo 17 blasted off from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida, bound for the moon.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: Standing alongside legendary astronauts like Neil Armstrong and Dick Gordon, a schoolboy from Lancashire was there to see the final manned lunar landing mission.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: Ahead of the screening of a documentary about his experience, Preston astronomer Dermot Gethings recalled how, at 16 years old, he was hand picked by the United States embassy and Nasa to witness the launch.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "As it launched there was this incredible adrenaline and a shockwave that rattled every bone in your body," said the now 70-year-old of the events of 7 December 1972.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "It is the stuff that you dream about." Dermot Gethings with Neil Armstrong at the Miami motel the pair stayed at ahead of the Apollo 17 launch While Gethings grew up in Frenchwood in Preston, he was shaped by the ongoing Cold War Space Race and the quest to put a man on the moon.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: A childhood of sci-fi, The Thunderbirds and televised Nasa missions meant space was always a keen interest of his.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: He said the "trigger moment" for his lifelong interest in astronomy was seeing the Milky Way in the night sky when he was 10.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "It hit me straight away - that was where I wanted to be," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "And I took a deep interest in space." From then on Gethings started an astronomy club at the former St John Fisher's School in Preston - putting on talks both at his school and others and running public exhibitions.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: Gethings got an O-Level in Astronomy, at age 16, after teaching himself the curriculum at home After Gethings' exhibitions were photographed by the Lancashire Evening Post, his life changed forever.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "A few months after the photographs were published I received a letter out of the blue from the United States Embassy in London," he recalled.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "It said 'We have a very special project to discuss with you regarding the forthcoming Apollo 17 mission'." Gethings was then told he was one of 16 UK students being invited for an interview at the embassy.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: One of the students was to be selected by Nasa for an all-expenses paid,19-day trip to watch Apollo 17's launch.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "I didn't hear anything for a couple of weeks," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: Gethings pictured in front of the White House on 5 December 1972 A memorable moment for Gethings came when he accidentally met Armstrong - the first man to have ever walked on the moon.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "On the day of the launch I stepped out of my motel room and clumsily walked into a tall gentleman," Gethings recalled.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "I stood on his foot by accident and I was really embarrassed.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "I looked up and the man smiling down at me was Neil Armstrong!" The pair walked downstairs together chatting about the upcoming launch, before Armstrong offered for his wife to take a photograph of them.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: They were only three miles (5km) away from the launchpad.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "My heart was pumping in my chest," he remembered.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "And when the vehicle cleared the tower suddenly you got punched in the chest by a shockwave.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "The ground beneath your feet was like an earthquake and the stands were rattling.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "And then you got hit by this incredibly painful crackling staccato snapping sound  against the skin on your face.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "Minutes later Apollo 17 became a bright star moving across the sky and away from us.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "The experience was something one never forgets or can be equalled." Gethings met and later received a postcard from Apollo 17 mission commander  Eugene Cernan During the 14-day mission the Apollo 17 astronauts, led by mission commander Eugene Cernan, performed three space walks on the lunar surface.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: The third moonwalk, on 13 December, was the last time anybody walked on the moon.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: Gethings was at the Space Center in Houston, Texas, when the astronauts on the moon's surface spoke directly to the group of students before collecting a moon rock from the surface.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: Once back on earth, that moonrock was split into 80 pieces - distributed to each student - and Gethings became the custodian of the UK's Apollo 17 Goodwill Moon Rock.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: The UK's Apollo 17 Goodwill Moon Rock is on display at the Natural History Museum in London When Gethings returned home he presented the moonrock to Prime Minister Edward Heath at 10 Downing Street in July 1973.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: Brigadier Jim McDivitt, Walter Annenberg, PM Edward Heath and Dermot Gethings at Downing Street Gethings has continued his love of astronomy ever since.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: A fellow of the Royal Astronomical Society and vice chair of Preston & District Astronomical Society, he also works with the Jeremiah Horrocks Institute of the University of Central Lancashire delivering talks.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: The story of his journey to becoming custodian of the UK's Apollo 17 Goodwill Moon Rock is set to be told in a 30-minute documentary by University of Lancashire graduate Sarah Bullough.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: Ahead of his big screen debut, Gethings said: "Space had been a passion all my life.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "To be brought over there to see places and meet people that you have only ever read about or seen on TV - it was the stuff of dreams.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "I knew what a privilege it was - even at the time.
sentences.article_title: 'I watched Apollo 17 launch with Neil Armstrong'

sentences.text: "It will just be fantastic to see that journey on the big screen." The Custodian of the Goodwill Moon Rock will be shown at the University's Preston Campus on Wednesday 14 October.

sentences.text: Chinstrap penguins get their name from a thin ring of feathers from ear to ear Almost two-thirds of the population of chinstrap penguins have disappeared from a remote volcanic island near Antarctica, aerial surveys suggest.

sentences.article_title: World's largest penguin colony hit by 'alarming' decline in numbers

sentences.article_title: World's largest penguin colony hit by 'alarming' decline in numbers

sentences.article_title: World's largest penguin colony hit by 'alarming' decline in numbers

sentences.text: The move comes six months after Epic Games confirmed it was laying off more than 1,000 employees Fortnite-maker Epic Games is making a "huge pivot" towards using artificial intelligence (AI) in its video game development, according to boss Tim Sweeney.
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: The US firm's CEO made the announcement on social media , external , saying developers are being moved to "retool for maximum AI acceleration".
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: It comes after Epic delayed the release of a collaboration with Disney featuring characters from Star Wars and Marvel, according to a report from Bloomberg , external .
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: BBC Newsbeat has approached Epic Games on its use of increased AI and the reported delay to its Disney project.
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: Details on that game are yet to be announced, but Bloomberg reported that developers were asked to use AI tools to finish it.
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: It said directors told staff "no more hand-written code" and are switching to having all the game's art "generated with full AI workflows".
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: Epic's founder and CEO Sweeney didn't publicly comment on the Disney collab, but did confirm further details around the company's use of AI in a series of posts on X.
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: He said the purpose wasn't "to do the same stuff with fewer people" but to give developers the tools to build "more" and "better stuff", something he called "empowering" for creators.
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: Critics of the decision reacted angrily to Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney's social media posts One response on Sweeney's X thread, which received 14,000 likes, accused him of not being able to read the room.
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: Sweeney responded by saying "much of the room wants it to be 2016, but it's not".
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: "Our job, as the provider of tools and technology to much of the industry, is to design for the present that is and the future that will soon be," he said.
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: Sweeney said ramping up the use of AI was a "modest aim to survive the AI revolution" and end up "making better code and content faster".
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: The news comes six months after Epic confirmed it was laying off more than 1,000 employees .
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: At the time, Sweeney attributed job cuts to a "downturn" in Fortnite engagement rather than AI.
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: Lisha Howen is in favour of AI being used to "help make things better", but says it shouldn't be used as a replacement The announcement brings a fresh focus to the long-running debate around the role of AI in the creative and arts sector .
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: Lisha Howen is a full-time game designer and says she "isn't completely against AI", but disagrees with it being used to fully generate artwork and graphics.
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: "I have friends who are game developers that use AI to aid them with writing code," says the 23-year-old, who doesn't work for Epic.
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: "And I have artists who don't use AI at all because artists, especially in the game industry, hate it because it's taking away their jobs.
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: "You can tell when something's been generated by AI, it looks terrible, it's cheap, and it's making people lose their jobs and lose their income." In 2025, actor union Sag-Aftra filed a complaint over the use of AI to recreate the voice of Star Wars villain Darth Vader in Fortnite.
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: She explains that while there is a "vocal minority" who play Fortnite, the core player base "don't really care about the external politics of it all".
sentences.article_title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI

sentences.text: "They'll just keep playing like nothing's changed." Listen to Newsbeat live at 12:45 and 17:45 weekdays - or listen back here .

sentences.text: Tom Cruise's latest film Digger is expected to lose around $245m (£185m), Hollywood analysts have said, after the film's continuing poor performance at the box office.

sentences.text: It brings Digger's total box office takings so far to around $35m (£26m) globally.

sentences.text: Gaten Matarazzo is no stranger to musical theatre Keeping your balance on a revolving stage probably sounds easy when you compare it with battling demogorgons, but Gaten Matarazzo points out one big difference.

sentences.article_title: Gaten Matarazzo on life after Stranger Things as he makes West End debut

sentences.text: The saga finally concluded last December after five seasons, and there's been interest in what the show's cast will do next.
sentences.article_title: Gaten Matarazzo on life after Stranger Things as he makes West End debut

sentences.text: "It's something you do inevitably step away from," says Matarazzo "We finished filming in 2024 - there's no more show to film.

sentences.text: "I still love what I do very much, I want to keep on doing it." Casting big names from TV and film in theatre shows is a growing trend, and one that sometimes provokes accusations of cashing in .

sentences.article_title: Gaten Matarazzo on life after Stranger Things as he makes West End debut

sentences.text: McGovern said he was shocked after visiting "appalling" facilities while researching the latest series of his BBC drama Time.

sentences.text: He told BBC North West Tonight those in young offender institutions (YOIs) were "banged up 23 hours a day" as part of a policy to stop offenders mixing, which gave officers an "excuse for being lazy".

sentences.text: The Prison Officers' Association (POA) said that criticism was "unfair" to call officers lazy - and the policy was essential due to a daily threat of serious violence.

sentences.text: Liverpool-born McGovern focused on adult prison estates in the first two series of BBC hit Time.
sentences.article_title: Jimmy McGovern claims young offender institution staff 'lazy'

sentences.text: But his third series, which sees a young cast star alongside David Tennant and Siobhan Finneran, follows young offenders through a system which McGovern said had "got to be better".

sentences.text: The new series stars Siobhan Finneran, Chukwubuikem Molokwu and David Tennant In researching the series, which he wrote with Samuel Bailey, McGovern decided to get a behind-the-scenes look inside real-life YOIs.
sentences.article_title: Jimmy McGovern claims young offender institution staff 'lazy'

sentences.text: He said what he witnessed left him "truly shocked".
sentences.article_title: Jimmy McGovern claims young offender institution staff 'lazy'

sentences.text: "It is absolutely appalling," he said.
sentences.article_title: Jimmy McGovern claims young offender institution staff 'lazy'

sentences.text: "There's young boys with enormous energy banged up 23 hours a day [and] not allowed out of the cells.
sentences.article_title: Jimmy McGovern claims young offender institution staff 'lazy'

sentences.text: "They call them rooms, but they're cells.
sentences.article_title: Jimmy McGovern claims young offender institution staff 'lazy'

sentences.text: "And that's because of the keep-apart system." The keep-aparts policy is a method of separating young offenders in a bid to cut down on violence.
sentences.article_title: Jimmy McGovern claims young offender institution staff 'lazy'

sentences.text: He said he believed the policy had allowed officers to avoid their duties.
sentences.article_title: Jimmy McGovern claims young offender institution staff 'lazy'

sentences.text: "It allows officers to sit on their backsides all day and do nothing," he said.
sentences.article_title: Jimmy McGovern claims young offender institution staff 'lazy'

sentences.text: "This happened before Covid, but Covid gave them the excuse to keep them banged up even more.
sentences.article_title: Jimmy McGovern claims young offender institution staff 'lazy'

sentences.text: "After Covid, they didn't want to see the kids, so it became worse." This video can not be played Watch the trailer for series 3 of Jimmy McGovern's drama Time He said he did not believe an increased use of the policy was due to staffing and funding challenges.
sentences.article_title: Jimmy McGovern claims young offender institution staff 'lazy'

sentences.text: "I'm afraid they're lazy," he said.
sentences.article_title: Jimmy McGovern claims young offender institution staff 'lazy'

sentences.text: "I've met wonderful prison officers, but I've seen some lazy ones and the keep-apart system enables them to be lazy with an excuse for being lazy." He said officers should be able to handle fights among the offenders and described conditions as "feral".
sentences.article_title: Jimmy McGovern claims young offender institution staff 'lazy'

sentences.text: "They're young boys bursting with energy [being] cooped up," he said.
sentences.article_title: Jimmy McGovern claims young offender institution staff 'lazy'

sentences.text: "When they get out, they want to fight, but [the staff] are prison officers.
sentences.article_title: Jimmy McGovern claims young offender institution staff 'lazy'

sentences.text: They should be able to handle that." He said he understood how "tough" the job was and that the young offenders in the facilities were "very, very difficult, so there has to be an element of regimentation [and] rules and regulations... but that's your job".

sentences.text: "I have the utmost respect for Jimmy's work [and] he is right to highlight the serious problems within young offender institutions," he said.

sentences.text: "YOIs are among the most violent prisons in the country.
